records.title: Rear Air Suspension Compressor and Air Spring Failure
records.description: The rear air ride suspension system fails frequently due to air spring leaks and compressor burnout. The air springs develop cracks in the rubber bladders, causing the rear to sag overnight. The compressor then runs continuously trying to maintain ride height, eventually burning itself out. This is extremely common after 80,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace both rear air springs and the compressor as a set. If the air lines have cracks, replace those too. Alternatively, convert to conventional coil springs and shocks with an air suspension bypass kit, which eliminates the problem permanently. The conversion kit costs less than one OEM air spring.

records.title: Transfer Case Encoder Motor and Position Sensor Failure
records.description: The transfer case encoder motor that controls AWD/4WD engagement fails, causing the "Service 4WD" message and preventing 4WD engagement. The position sensor inside the encoder motor sends incorrect signals. The transfer case may also develop an internal fluid leak past the front output seal.
records.solution: Replace the encoder motor on the transfer case. The motor is externally mounted and accessible. After replacement, a transfer case relearn procedure must be performed with a scan tool. Check and top off the transfer case fluid with the correct Auto-Trak II fluid.

records.title: Power Liftgate Strut Failure and Liftgate Falling
records.description: The power liftgate on the Escalade ESV is prone to gas strut failure due to the extra-long and heavy liftgate (longer than standard Escalade). The struts lose pressure and the liftgate won't stay open or falls unexpectedly. The power liftgate motor and latch can also fail, preventing the gate from opening or closing electrically. This is a safety hazard as the heavy gate can fall on passengers loading cargo.
records.solution: Replace both liftgate gas struts together — they are inexpensive ($30-60/pair) and easy to replace with a flathead screwdriver to pop the ball studs. If the power liftgate motor has failed, the motor assembly (GM 25965765) requires interior trim panel removal but is a 1-hour DIY job. Lubricate latch mechanism with white lithium grease annually.
symptoms: Liftgate won't stay open or slowly falls down
Power liftgate opens partway then stops
Liftgate makes grinding noise when operating electrically
Must manually hold liftgate open while loading

citations.description: Escalade ESV liftgate strut failure reports

communityRecommendations.content: Stabilus SG130098 liftgate gas struts (pair) — direct OEM replacement for ESV-length liftgate
Always replace both struts together even if only one appears weak — the other will fail shortly after
Use a prop rod when working under the liftgate if struts are weak — the ESV liftgate is extremely heavy and can cause serious injury

records.title: Autoride Air Suspension Compressor and Shock Failure
records.description: The Escalade ESV equipped with the Autoride electronic air suspension system experiences compressor burnout and air shock/strut failure. The compressor runs excessively trying to compensate for leaking air shocks, eventually overheating and failing. Replacement OEM air shocks are extremely expensive, and the compressor costs $800+ from the dealer. This affects the rear air shocks most commonly but front electronic struts also fail.
records.solution: The most popular and cost-effective solution is converting to passive coil spring suspension using an Arnott or Strutmasters conversion kit. This eliminates the air compressor, air shocks, and height sensors. A bypass module suppresses the Autoride warning lights. Alternatively, replace with new OEM or Arnott air shocks and a new compressor.
symptoms: Vehicle sitting low on one or both rear corners
Air compressor running constantly (buzzing from rear)
Service Ride Control message on DIC
Vehicle drops to bump stops after sitting overnight

citations.description: Escalade Autoride suspension failure and conversion guide
ESV air suspension compressor burnout thread

communityRecommendations.content: Strutmasters Escalade ESV air suspension conversion kit — converts to passive springs, eliminates all Autoride components
If keeping air suspension, replace the compressor relay first ($15) — a stuck relay causes 90% of compressor burnouts
A failed air suspension compressor can leave the vehicle on the bump stops — do not drive in this condition as it destroys tire sidewalls and is unstable

records.title: 10-Speed 10L80/10L90 Harsh Shifting, Shudder, and Valve Body Control Solenoid Issues
records.description: Owners have reported harsh 1-2 or 2-1 shifts, delayed engagement, shudder, and transmission warning messages on the current-generation Escalade ESV. GM service information and field reports point to valve body/control solenoid faults, internal transmission control valve issues, and software calibration concerns on 10-speed units used in full-size SUVs. Some vehicles require valve body replacement, while others progress to more extensive transmission repair.
records.solution: Diagnosis should include scanning for transmission control DTCs, checking adaptive values, verifying fluid condition, and following GM bulletin procedures for valve body and control solenoid performance. Dealers commonly perform TCM calibration updates first; persistent cases may need valve body replacement or internal transmission repair. Road testing both cold and hot is important because many complaints are intermittent early on.

citations.title: GM TSB/Service Information for 10-speed harsh shift and valve body concerns

communityRecommendations.content: Ask the dealer to check for the latest TCM calibration before authorizing major transmission work.

records.title: 6.2L L87 Connecting Rod/Bearing Failure Leading to Engine Seizure
records.description: Multiple owners of 2021-2024 Escalade/Escalade ESV models with the 6.2L L87 V8 have reported sudden engine failure, knocking, loss of power, and complete seizure. GM issued a safety recall covering certain vehicles for manufacturing defects that can damage connecting rods and crankshaft components, often resulting in catastrophic engine failure with little warning. Owner complaints describe failures both at low mileage and during highway driving, creating a significant safety concern.
records.solution: Diagnosis typically includes checking for rod knock, low oil pressure, metal debris in the oil, and engine lock-up. GM's recall procedure involves inspection and, where required, engine replacement or repair per factory guidance. Vehicles not yet failed but included in campaign population should be checked by VIN immediately and should not be ignored if any knocking or oil-pressure warnings appear.

records.title: Intermittent No-Start, Battery Drain, and Control Module Sleep/Wake Electrical Faults
records.description: A recurring complaint on 2021+ Escalade ESV models is a dead battery or no-start condition after sitting overnight or for a few days. Owners and technicians have linked these events to parasitic draw from modules that fail to go to sleep, telematics/infotainment wake-up behavior, and occasional battery or charging-system management faults. Some vehicles need repeated dealer visits because the drain is intermittent and difficult to capture.
records.solution: Proper diagnosis requires a parasitic draw test after all modules should be asleep, battery state-of-health testing, and checking for software updates related to telematics, radio, and body control modules. Repairs may include battery replacement, module reprogramming, fuse-isolation of the offending circuit, or replacement of a faulty control module. Because low voltage can trigger many unrelated warnings, the battery and charging system should be verified first.
symptoms: multiple warning lights after jump start

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for 2021 Cadillac Escalade ESV battery drain and no-start issues

communityRecommendations.content: Owners recommend getting a printed parasitic draw report from the dealer because intermittent drains are often dismissed if the battery is simply recharged.
If the vehicle sits for long periods, a quality AGM-compatible maintainer can help prevent repeated deep discharge while diagnosis is pending.

records.title: OLED Curved Display Blackout, Flicker, and Infotainment Module Failures
records.description: The 38-inch curved OLED display system in the 2021+ Escalade ESV has generated repeated owner complaints for black screens, flickering, frozen infotainment, loss of backup camera image, and intermittent gauge display issues. Reports point to software instability, communication faults between display/control modules, and occasional hardware replacement of the radio or display assembly. Because key vehicle functions are integrated into the screen, failures can affect usability and safety features.
records.solution: Diagnosis usually starts with checking for module communication faults, verifying battery voltage stability, and applying the latest infotainment software updates. Some vehicles are fixed with module reprogramming or hard resets, while persistent cases require replacement of the display, radio/HMI module, or related harness components. If the backup camera or driver information display is affected, the issue should be treated as more than a convenience problem.

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for 2021 Cadillac Escalade ESV electrical/display failures

communityRecommendations.content: Before replacing parts, owners suggest documenting whether the failure happens after remote start, after OTA updates, or during low battery voltage events.
If the screen is intermittently blank, ask the dealer to check for radio/HMI software updates and bulletin coverage rather than only rebooting the system.

records.title: Super Cruise and Driver Assistance System Faults from Camera/Radar Module Errors
records.description: Owners have reported repeated 'Service Driver Assist System,' 'Super Cruise Unavailable,' and related warnings on current-generation Escalade ESV models. Problems are commonly tied to front camera calibration faults, radar sensor communication issues, software bugs, or poor module alignment after windshield work or minor front-end impacts. In some cases adaptive cruise, lane keeping, automatic emergency braking, and Super Cruise become unavailable until repaired.
records.solution: Diagnosis should include scanning all ADAS modules for communication and calibration faults, inspecting radar/camera mounting, and verifying windshield condition and camera aim. Repairs may involve software updates, camera or radar replacement, connector repair, or full recalibration using OEM targets. After windshield replacement, proper calibration is essential to avoid recurring warnings.

communityRecommendations.content: If warnings started after windshield replacement, owners strongly recommend confirming OEM calibration was performed, not just glass installation.
Keep the front camera area and radar cover clean and photograph warning messages before key-cycling the vehicle.
